name: Payroll KYC and beneficiary screening do not prove worker identity continuity

attribution.legal_posture: Financial anomalies are review signals; identity, facilitation, and DPRK attribution require other evidence. First-party platform control or threat-research guidance is normalized as defensive context; control-effectiveness status requires separate validation; Sophos-published payroll and finance guidance.

caveats: Apply controls consistently with privacy, employment, labor, accessibility, retention, notice, correction, and access-governance requirements.
Lawful financial products require risk-based policy, legal review, and documented exceptions rather than prohibition by brand or worker location.
Financial data is sensitive. Minimize access and avoid exposing raw bank, tax, or payment identifiers in threat-intelligence outputs.
Joint accounts, payroll providers, relocation, name changes, bank mergers, failed payments, and contractor intermediaries can be legitimate.
KYC, sanctions screening, and beneficiary checks establish screening results; work performance and continuous account control require additional evidence.

These controls address submitted identity, account, and beneficiary checks; identifying the true worker who controls the submitted identity, account, or beneficiary requires separate evidence. Deel publishes a general control description, and no DPRK-specific detection count is published here.
Use the pattern to prioritize documented human-led review; DPRK affiliation, fraud, and malicious intent require a combined evidence record.

statements: Build a governed employee-beneficiary graph and alert on newly shared or rapidly changing beneficiary attributes across otherwise unrelated workers or contractors.
Correlate payroll changes with HR identity events, endpoint/device changes, location claims, manager confirmation, and approved exceptions.
Require secondary-channel verification and dual authorization for sensitive beneficiary changes, preserving an auditable override trail.
limitations: Joint accounts, payroll providers, relocation, name changes, bank mergers, failed payments, and contractor intermediaries can be legitimate.
Do not prohibit lawful financial products solely by brand or worker location; use risk-based policy, legal review, and documented exceptions.
Financial data is sensitive. Minimize access and avoid exposing raw bank, tax, or payment identifiers in threat-intelligence outputs.

statements: Deel states that it performs KYC on platform customers, screens transactions and beneficiaries against sanctions and anti-fraud lists, applies enhanced due diligence to businesses, refreshes checks, and contractually prohibits platform access from North Korea and transactions involving restricted parties.
limitations: These controls do not prove the true worker controls the submitted identity, account, or beneficiary, and Deel publishes no DPRK-specific detection count here.
